newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 16.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Peters wants all to save $160,000: The compulsory superannuation scheme New Zealanders will vote on later this year would probably be an annuity scheme, Treasurer Winston Peters indicated on Tuesday. Page 1.

McKinnon admits hasty in recall: Foreign Affairs Don McKinnon admitted on Tuesday that his decision to recall the ambassador to Iran, Daniel Richards, had been more than hastily because he had been in Germany rather than New Zealand. Page 1.

Labour MP demands apology from Sowry: Labour MP Annette King is demanding an apology from Social Welfare Minister Roger Sowry for his denial of her claim that a teenage runaway was placed in the care of a woman staying at a Porirua brothel. Page 1.
ACT backs petition to stop building for ministers: ACT NZ is backing a petition by Auckland woman Susan Grimsdell to stop a new $94 million building for Cabinet ministers going ahead. Page 2.
Poll shows fall in party support for National: Support for the National Party dropped six points to 41 percent in the latest One Network News/Colmar Brunton poll out on Tuesday night. Page 2.

Failed library project 'too big': The minister responsible for the National Library, Wyatt Creech, has criticised the National Library for having got involved in a computer project that was developing new software rather than using existing technology. Page 2.
Lower drinking age resisted: The Health Ministry advised against dropping the minimum drinking age in its submission to the Sale of Liquor Review Panel. Page 2.

Quarterly inflation drop biggest in 36 years: Interest rates and the New Zealand dollar could continue to fall in the wake of the biggest quarterly drop in inflation for 36 years, analysts said on Tuesday. Page 12.

East Coast oil venture 'encouraging': There are encouraging signs of an oil or gas field with up to 50 million barrels of hydrocarbons on the East Coast around Wairoa, according to joint venture explorers gas retailer Enerco and join venture partner Westech Energy. Page 12.
Friday deadline for offer on Defiance: Brazilian-based Bunge Foods Queensland has till Friday under Australian law to alter its offer to New Zealand and Australian shareholders in Defiance. Page 12.
Loss on sale for Goodman: Goodman Fielder has forecast an extraordinary loss of A$15 million on the sale of its European milling and baking business Meneba NV. Page 12.
CBD plans NZ$29 million public issue: Commercial property company CBD New Zealand planned a public issue of shares to raise $29.5 million, chairman Graeme Horsley said on Tuesday. Page 13.

CHHP expects plastics buy to boost exports: Exports to Australia by Cater Holt Harvey Packagaing and sales in New Zealand should be boosted by the company's acquisition of a plastics manufacturer in Sydney, CHHP chief executive Doug McKay said on Tuesday. Page 13.
Slump in Steel and Tube activity lowers profit pick: Steel and Tube Holdings said on Tuesday its profit for the six months to May 31 was likely to be lower than it had forecast. Page 13.
Deal reached on Strait cable cost: Power generator ECNZ and national grid operator Trans Power have reached agreement on sharing costs of the Cook Strait cable, ending months of wrangling. Page 13.

Housing saving 'increasing': Households are voluntarily saving at an increasing rate ahead of any decision on compulsory superannuation, according to the Westpac-FPG household savings indicators for 1996. Page 14.

Ex-Works Ministry embarks on new growth path: Works Consultancy Services changed its name last week to Opus International Consultants. The move follows the sale of Works last year to listed Malaysian company Kinta Kellas for $45.8 million, and ends the notional link Works had with the old Ministry of Works. Page 15.
Housing affordability improves in March: Housing affordability picked up strongly in the March quarter, according to Massey University's home mortgage affordability index. Page 15.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Police admit $50m hi-tech punt: Jobs lost in wait for windfall from shaky system: Police hope to reap $50 million from their troubled crime-fighting computer by selling the "world first" system to other countries.

Heavy rain brings EMCO some relief on lake levels: The risk of another 1992-style winter power crisis is receding with heavier than normal rainfall this month replenishing the South Island's hydro lakes.

Inflation figures send interest rates tumbling: The old market adage of "buy the rumour, sell the fact" was tossed aside on New Zealand financial markets on Tuesday as investors just kept on buying after the release of better than expected inflation figures for the March quarter.
Ernest Adams adds new chief exec to mix: Food group Ernest Adams has found one of the final ingredients for an 18-month management reshuffle with the appointment of Tony Glass as chief executive.

Progressive challenged to deliver the goods: Realignmnent move expected to ignite price wars: Progressive Enterprises will need to deliver on its promises if its share price is to maintain its upward momentum.

Directors' legal risks overstated says US lawyer: People have overstated the vulnerability of directors to legal action for taking even normal business risks under new company law, says a United States lawyer.

Taranaki methanol boosts production: Vancouver-based Methanex increased its Taranaki methanol production to 649,000 tonnes in the March quarter, from 357,000 tonnes in March 1996, as international prices rose due to a combination of increased demand and outages at competitors' plants.

Roller in technicial breach of listing: Listed flour miller turned tourist operator, Roller International, is technically in breach of Stock Exchange listing requirements after its two major shareholders lifted their combined stake in the company to 54.4 percent.

Cellular future under study: Next week, a group of high-minded individuals will meet in Wellington to grapple with inpenetrable acronyms, incomprehensible jargon, and, while they are at it, the shape of the next generation of cellular telephony in New Zealand.

Bank disclosure scheme leaves academic puzzled: The squeeze on banks' lending margins in the final quarter of 1996 provides a puzzle not explained by their Reserve Bank-man-dated disclosure documents, a Massey University banking expert says.

Evergreen issue wins shareholder approval: Evergreen Forests shareholders on Tuesday approved the placement of up to 33 million shares with investors in the United States and elsewhere at 55 cents a share.
National Bank bonds to rival Govt stock: The National Bank is to issue bonds in its own name for sale to retail investors in competition with government bonds.
THE PRESS

Polls puts Peters at new low: Treasurer Winston Peters outlined plans for a compulsory savings scheme on Tuesday as a new poll put his rating in the leaders' popularity stakes at three percent. Page 1.
CPI - 0.3 percent March quarter takes markets by surprise: A merchant banker on Tuesday criticised the Consumers Price Index survey as outdated. Page 27.
Dollar eases, bonds dip on back of data: The New Zealand dollar closed just under half a US cent down on Tuesday after the low inflation figures announced on Tuesday. Page 27.
Blue Star moves for Wang: Blue Star Systems said on Tuesday that it was moving to acquire compulsorily the shares it did not already own in Wang NZ. Page 28.
Kiwi Gold issue approved: Mineral exploration company Kiwi Gold's shareholders on Tuesday approved the issue and allotment of 25.1 million shares and the same number of options. Page 28.
NZ Light Leathers confident: New Zealand Light Leathers is confident of repeating its 1996 profit in 1997. Page 29.
Steel, Tube clips forecast: The directors of Steel and Tube Holdings on Tuesday downgraded the Wellington-based engineering group's expected result. Page 29.
Warrant issued: Challenger Asset Management, an Australian private funds manager, has started a new type of warrant, which will be issued by Australia's Macquarie Bank. Page 29.
